file_path.description: publish: the local page Claude publishes (.html, or .md only when a skill says so). For an Artifact created from an Artifact type, it is one of that Artifact's data files. With `asset: true`, it is the local file Claude uploads. A short, distinctive basename also serves as the title when nothing else gives one.

asset.description: publish with `url`: true uploads `file_path` (or each of `file_paths`) to that artifact's asset store instead of publishing it as the page — or, with `from_url` and `asset_ids` in place of `file_path`, copies those assets of another artifact into it server side (see **Calls**).

file_paths.description: publish with `asset: true` only: several local image, video, PDF, font, stylesheet or script files in place of `file_path`, up to 25 in one call, all into the artifact that `url` names; one approval covers the call, and the result lists each file's id and url, or why it was not uploaded. A CSV, Markdown, JSON or plain-text file, a symbolic or hard link, and a file outside the working directory each go in a call of their own with `file_path`.

from_url.description: publish with `asset: true`, in place of `file_path`: the SOURCE artifact's claude.ai URL — one the person can open.

asset_ids.description: publish with `asset: true` and `from_url` only: 1–10 distinct asset ids from the source artifact (from a `scope: "assets"` listing of it, or an upload result).

favicon.description: Deprecated; Claude omits it and uses `icon`.

icon.description: One short generic word for the artifact's browser-tab icon, such as chart, calendar, recipe, code or map: a plain signifier, never a product or brand name. Claude includes it on every page's first publish and omits it on a redeploy so the artifact keeps its icon, passing a new one only when the person asks. Ignored on an Artifact created from an Artifact type.

files.description: Supporting files to publish alongside the page, as a map {"published/path": "source/path" | {from, contentType} | {artifact, path, ver?} | null}. The key is what the HTML references. The source is a path on disk, or {from, contentType} when the type cannot be inferred from the published extension. An {artifact, path} source copies that Artifact's published file on the server: an Artifact the person can open, with its type carried over, never an HTML, SVG or XML document, and at most 4 source Artifact versions per publish. null removes that path on an update, and files left out are kept. A plain list publishes each file at its own spelling. Sources must be under the working directory or Claude's scratchpad directory. `preflight.js` at the artifact root is reserved: it runs against open pages when Claude publishes updates, and it must be a JavaScript module of at most 8 KiB whose default export is a function, or the publish is refused.

path.description: Path relative to the working directory (or to `root`, which may be a folder in your scratchpad directory); the file is served at this same path next to the page.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the extension for common types (css/js/json/png/…) — pass explicitly otherwise.

from.description: Source file path — relative to `root` (default: the working directory), or absolute under the working directory or your scratchpad directory.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the PUBLISHED extension for common types — pass explicitly otherwise.

artifact.description: Another artifact's claude.ai URL: the file is copied from ITS published files, server side — nothing is downloaded. You must be able to open that artifact.

path.description: The file's published path inside that Artifact, as a listing of its files prints it (not "index.html").

ver.description: A version of that Artifact to copy from instead of its current one — only versions you are served (its history, if you can edit it); omit for the current version.

root.description: The base directory that relative `files` sources resolve against, like a bundler root. It never changes published paths. It is relative to the working directory, or absolute within it or within Claude's scratchpad directory. It requires `files`, except on an Artifact made from a type, where a data `file_path` under it is served at its path relative to it.

pin.description: publish only: true also pins the published artifact to the person's claude.ai sidebar once it is published. Claude passes it only when the person asked for that. A failed pin never fails the publish, and the result says so.

limit.description: list only: the maximum number of artifacts to return (default 25).

scope.description: list: which listing to return. 'mine' is the default. The others are 'shared', 'all', 'types', 'files' (with `url`) and 'assets' (with `url`, continued with `after`). See **Calls**.

type_query.description: list with scope 'types' only: limits the listing to the types whose title or description match this text best, ignoring case; a type that matches less well is left out, so a narrowed listing is not the whole catalog. Claude omits it when choosing a type for a request, unless a listing made without it says more types exist than it shows.

type.description: list only: the name of a published Artifact type, as a 'types' listing shows it (case does not matter). The listing then shows the Artifacts made from that type instead of the person's gallery. Claude passes this or `type_url`, not both.

intent.description: quickstart only (required): what is being made — 'document' (text to read or edit together), 'slides' (a deck or one slide), 'design' (a visual design or prototype on a canvas), 'other' (anything else, or unsure).

design_systems.description: quickstart only: false when a design system's link is already in hand (it is then read with its own call) or one was declined. Omitted or true, the result lists the design systems (not for a document) and, for slides or a design, attaches the default one's README.

title.description: publish: the fallback title for an HTML page whose file has no <title>. It is a name, not a summary, and Claude keeps it the same across redeploys. On a `type_url` create, it is the new Artifact's name: what the person called it, or a short descriptive name. If it is left out, the Artifact is named after the type.

description.description: publish: one sentence for the subtitle on the gallery card.

label.description: A short name for this publish, at most 60 characters (e.g. "Draft to legal"). Optional. It is a few words, not a description.

overwrite_unread.description: publish with `files` or `root` to an existing artifact: published paths this call may replace or remove although you have not read or listed them in this session. Every other path the call touches must be one you read by its `path`, saw in a file listing, or published yourself, and must not have changed since — otherwise nothing is sent and the refusal names each path. Name a path here only when the user asked for it to be replaced without looking at what is there; it never excuses a path that changed after you read it.

url.description: An existing artifact's claude.ai URL. On a publish, it is the artifact to update in place, which must be one the person owns or was given edit access to (a read of it says "writer"); Claude omits it for a new artifact or a redeploy in the same conversation (see **To update an artifact from an earlier conversation**). For read, delete and the other calls that take a URL, it is the artifact to act on.

type_url.description: publish: the Artifact type to create this new, private Artifact from (a link from a 'types' listing). Claude omits `url`. Any `file_path`/`files` passed become the new Artifact's own files beside the type's fixed ones. read (no `url`): the type to describe. list: the type whose Artifacts to list, or Claude names the type with `type` instead.

auto_open.description: Only with `type_url` and no `file_path`: when the new Artifact opens for the person. Claude passes "after_first_write" when it will fill the Artifact right after creating it with a files publish to its url, so the person does not first see it empty. The Artifact then opens on that first write. Otherwise Claude omits it, and the Artifact opens when created; Claude always omits it for a type whose content it writes through a connector, such as a Claude Docs document, since no publish or store write follows to open it.

prompt.description: read, for an artifact shared with the person: what Claude needs from it, which steers the isolated summary.

force.description: publish: a last-resort overwrite that **discards** the newer published version. On a conflict, Claude merges its changes onto the newer content that the rejection hands it and publishes again. Claude passes true only when the person explicitly said to discard that specific version, and the server may still refuse it over a version saved from inside the page.

out_dir.description: read with `path`: the directory to save into. The default is this artifact's folder in Claude's scratchpad directory, where saving needs no approval. A published file lands at <out_dir>/<published path>, and saving it outside that default folder asks the person first. An asset's file is named by its id plus its type's extension; saving it outside the default folder is an ordinary file save the person may be asked to approve.

path.description: read: the file's published path inside the artifact, exactly as a 'files' listing printed it ("index.html" is the page itself). The file is saved locally, the result says where, and a small text file's contents are included. It can instead be an uploaded asset's id (32 hex characters, from an 'assets' listing or an upload result), and that asset is saved to a local file. delete: the id of the one asset to remove.

paths.description: read: several published paths in place of `path`, up to 256 in one call. Each file is saved as a single `path` would be, and the result lists where each one landed, or why it could not be read, with small text files' contents included while they fit.

after.description: list with scope 'assets' only: the `next` value from a previous listing, passed to continue it.

page.description: read only: true returns the rendered page in cases where a read otherwise returns something else. A typed Artifact's read leaves out the type's own page.

capabilities.description: publish: the runtime capabilities this page declares, as {name: config}. Claude loads the `artifact-capabilities` skill before passing it. On a redeploy Claude omits the field to keep what the page has, and {} clears it.

contract.description: publish: the artifact's runtime version. Leaving it out keeps the current version (the default), 'latest' upgrades, and an exact version pins or rolls back. It changes how the published page behaves, so Claude passes it only when the author explicitly intends that change.

tools.name: AskUserQuestion
tools.description:
Use this tool only when you are blocked on a decision that is genuinely the user's to make: one you cannot resolve from the request, the code, or sensible defaults.

Usage notes:
- Users will always be able to select "Other" to provide custom text input
- Use multiSelect: true to allow multiple answers to be selected for a question
- If you recommend a specific option, make that the first option in the list and add "(Recommended)" at the end of the label

Plan mode note: To switch into plan mode, use EnterPlanMode (not this tool). Once in plan mode, use this tool to clarify requirements or choose between approaches BEFORE finalizing your plan. Do NOT use this tool to ask "Is my plan ready?", "Should I proceed?", or otherwise reference "the plan" in questions — the user cannot see the plan until you call ExitPlanMode for approval.

Preview feature:
Use the optional `preview` field on options when presenting concrete artifacts that users need to visually compare:
- ASCII mockups of UI layouts or components
- Code snippets showing different implementations
- Diagram variations
- Configuration examples

Preview content is rendered as markdown in a monospace box. Multi-line text with newlines is supported. When any option has a preview, the UI switches to a side-by-side layout with a vertical option list on the left and preview on the right. Do not use previews for simple preference questions where labels and descriptions suffice. Note: previews are only supported for single-select questions (not multiSelect).

questions.description: Questions to ask the user (1-4 questions)

question.description: The complete question to ask the user. Should be clear, specific, and end with a question mark. Example: "Which library should we use for date formatting?" If multiSelect is true, phrase it accordingly, e.g. "Which features do you want to enable?"

header.description: Very short label displayed as a chip/tag (max 12 chars). Examples: "Auth method", "Library", "Approach".

options.description: The available choices for this question. Must have 2-4 options. Each option should be a distinct, mutually exclusive choice (unless multiSelect is enabled). There should be no 'Other' option, that will be provided automatically.

label.description: The display text for this option that the user will see and select. Should be concise (1-5 words) and clearly describe the choice.

description.description: Explanation of what this option means or what will happen if chosen. Useful for providing context about trade-offs or implications.

preview.description: Optional preview content rendered when this option is focused. Use for mockups, code snippets, or visual comparisons that help users compare options. See the tool description for the expected content format.

multiSelect.description: Set to true to allow the user to select multiple options instead of just one. Use when choices are not mutually exclusive.

answers.description: User answers collected by the permission component

annotations.description: Optional per-question annotations from the user (e.g., notes on preview selections). Keyed by question text.

preview.description: The preview content of the selected option, if the question used previews.

notes.description: Free-text notes the user added to their selection.

metadata.description: Optional metadata for tracking and analytics purposes. Not displayed to user.

source.description: Optional identifier for the source of this question (e.g., "remember" for /remember command). Used for analytics tracking.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a given bash command and returns its output.

The working directory persists between commands, but shell state does not. The shell environment is initialized from the user's profile (bash or zsh).

IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user:

 - Read files: Use Read (NOT cat/head/tail)
 - Edit files: Use Edit (NOT sed/awk)
 - Write files: Use Write (NOT echo >/cat <<EOF)
 - Communication: Output text directly (NOT echo/printf)
While the Bash tool can do similar things, it’s better to use the built-in tools as they provide a better user experience and make it easier to review tool calls and give permission.

# Instructions
 - If your command will create new directories or files, first use this tool to run `ls` to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location.
 - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes in your command (e.g., cd "path with spaces/file.txt")
 - Try to maintain your current working directory throughout the session by using absolute paths and avoiding usage of `cd`. You may use `cd` if the User explicitly requests it. In particular, never prepend `cd <current-directory>` to a `git` command — `git` already operates on the current working tree, and the compound triggers a permission prompt.
 - You may specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes). By default, your command will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
 - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes. You do not need to use '&' at the end of the command when using this parameter.
 - For git commands:
  - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
  - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
  - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.
 - Avoid unnecessary `sleep` commands:
  - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
  - Use the Monitor tool to stream events from a background process (each stdout line is a notification). For one-shot "wait until done," use Bash with run_in_background instead.
  - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — use `run_in_background`. No sleep needed.
  - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause.
  - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
  - Long leading `sleep` commands are blocked. To poll until a condition is met, use Monitor with an until-loop (e.g. `until <check>; do sleep 2; done`) — you get a notification when the loop exits. Do not chain shorter sleeps to work around the block.
 - When running `find`, search from `.` (or a specific path), not `/` — scanning the full filesystem can exhaust system resources on large trees.
 - When using `find -regex` with alternation, put the longest alternative first. Example: use `'.*\.\(tsx\|ts\)'` not `'.*\.\(ts\|tsx\)'` — the second form silently skips `.tsx` files.


# Committing changes with git

Only create commits when requested by the user. If unclear, ask first. When the user asks you to create a new git commit, follow these steps carefully:

You can call multiple tools in a single response. When multiple independent pieces of information are requested and all commands are likely to succeed, run multiple tool calls in parallel for optimal performance. The numbered steps below indicate which commands should be batched in parallel.

Git Safety Protocol:
- NEVER update the git config
- NEVER run destructive git commands (push --force, reset --hard, checkout ., restore ., clean -f, branch -D) unless the user explicitly requests these actions. Taking unauthorized destructive actions is unhelpful and can result in lost work, so it's best to ONLY run these commands when given direct instructions 
- NEVER skip hooks (--no-verify, --no-gpg-sign, etc) unless the user explicitly requests it
- NEVER run force push to main/master, warn the user if they request it
- CRITICAL: Always create NEW commits rather than amending, unless the user explicitly requests a git amend. When a pre-commit hook fails, the commit did NOT happen — so --amend would modify the PREVIOUS commit, which may result in destroying work or losing previous changes. Instead, after hook failure, fix the issue, re-stage, and create a NEW commit
- When staging files, prefer adding specific files by name rather than using "git add -A" or "git add .", which can accidentally include sensitive files (.env, credentials) or large binaries
- NEVER commit changes unless the user explicitly asks you to. It is VERY IMPORTANT to only commit when explicitly asked, otherwise the user will feel that you are being too proactive

1. Run the following bash commands in parallel, each using the Bash tool:
  - Run a git status command to see all untracked files. IMPORTANT: Never use the -uall flag as it can cause memory issues on large repos.
  - Run a git diff command to see both staged and unstaged changes that will be committed.
  - Run a git log command to see recent commit messages, so that you can follow this repository's commit message style.
2. Analyze all staged changes (both previously staged and newly added) and draft a commit message:
  - Summarize the nature of the changes (eg. new feature, enhancement to an existing feature, bug fix, refactoring, test, docs, etc.). Ensure the message accurately reflects the changes and their purpose (i.e. "add" means a wholly new feature, "update" means an enhancement to an existing feature, "fix" means a bug fix, etc.).
  - Do not commit files that likely contain secrets (.env, credentials.json, etc). Warn the user if they specifically request to commit those files
  - Draft a concise (1-2 sentences) commit message that focuses on the "why" rather than the "what"
  - Ensure it accurately reflects the changes and their purpose
3. Run the following commands in parallel:
   - Add relevant untracked files to the staging area.
   - Create the commit with a message, ending with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.
   - Run git status after the commit completes to verify success.
   Note: git status depends on the commit completing, so run it sequentially after the commit.
4. If the commit fails due to pre-commit hook: fix the issue and create a NEW commit

Important notes:
- NEVER run additional commands to read or explore code, besides git bash commands
- NEVER use the TaskCreate or Agent tools
- DO NOT push to the remote repository unless the user explicitly asks you to do so
- IMPORTANT: Never use git commands with the -i flag (like git rebase -i or git add -i) since they require interactive input which is not supported.
- IMPORTANT: Do not use --no-edit with git rebase commands, as the --no-edit flag is not a valid option for git rebase.
- If there are no changes to commit (i.e., no untracked files and no modifications), do not create an empty commit
- In order to ensure good formatting, ALWAYS pass the commit message via a HEREDOC, a la this example:
<example>
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
   Commit message here.
   EOF
   )"
</example>

# Creating pull requests
Use the gh command via the Bash tool for ALL GitHub-related tasks including working with issues, pull requests, checks, and releases. If given a Github URL use the gh command to get the information needed.

IMPORTANT: When the user asks you to create a pull request, follow these steps carefully:

1. Run the following bash commands in parallel using the Bash tool, in order to understand the current state of the branch since it diverged from the main branch:
   - Run a git status command to see all untracked files (never use -uall flag)
   - Run a git diff command to see both staged and unstaged changes that will be committed
   - Check if the current branch tracks a remote branch and is up to date with the remote, so you know if you need to push to the remote
   - Run a git log command and `git diff [base-branch]...HEAD` to understand the full commit history for the current branch (from the time it diverged from the base branch)
2. Analyze all changes that will be included in the pull request, making sure to look at all relevant commits (NOT just the latest commit, but ALL commits that will be included in the pull request!!!), and draft a pull request title and summary:
   - Keep the PR title short (under 70 characters)
   - Use the description/body for details, not the title
3. Run the following commands in parallel:
   - Create new branch if needed
   - Push to remote with -u flag if needed
   - Create PR using gh pr create with the format below. Use a HEREDOC to pass the body to ensure correct formatting. End the body with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.
<example>
gh pr create --title "the pr title" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary
<1-3 bullet points>

## Test plan
[Bulleted markdown checklist of TODOs for testing the pull request...]
EOF
)"
</example>

Important:
- DO NOT use the TaskCreate or Agent tools
- Return the PR URL when you're done, so the user can see it

# Other common operations
- View comments on a Github PR: gh api repos/foo/bar/pulls/123/comments

   - Create PR using gh pr create with the format below. Use a HEREDOC to pass the body to ensure correct formatting. End the body with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.
<example>
gh pr create --title "the pr title" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary
<1-3 bullet points>

## Test plan
[Bulleted markdown checklist of TODOs for testing the pull request...]
EOF
)"
</example>

Important:
- DO NOT use the TaskCreate or Agent tools
- Return the PR URL when you're done, so the user can see it

# Other common operations
- View comments on a Github PR: gh api repos/foo/bar/pulls/123/comments

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacements in files.

Usage:
- You must use your `Read` tool at least once in the conversation before editing. This tool will error if you attempt an edit without reading the file.
- When editing text from Read tool output, ensure you preserve the exact indentation (tabs/spaces) as it appears AFTER the line number prefix. The line number prefix format is: line number + tab. Everything after that is the actual file content to match. Never include any part of the line number prefix in the old_string or new_string.
- ALWAYS prefer editing existing files in the codebase. NEVER write new files unless explicitly required.
- Only use emojis if the user explicitly requests it. Avoid adding emojis to files unless asked.
- The edit will FAIL if `old_string` is not unique in the file. Either provide a larger string with more surrounding context to make it unique or use `replace_all` to change every instance of `old_string`.
- Use `replace_all` for replacing and renaming strings across the file. This parameter is useful if you want to rename a variable for instance.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem. You can access any file directly by using this tool.
Assume this tool is able to read all files on the machine. If the User provides a path to a file assume that path is valid. It is okay to read a file that does not exist; an error will be returned.

Usage:
- The file_path parameter must be an absolute path, not a relative path
- By default, it reads up to 2000 lines starting from the beginning of the file
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- This tool allows Claude Code to read images (eg PNG, JPG, etc). When reading an image file the contents are presented visually as Claude Code is a multimodal LLM.
- This tool can read PDF files (.pdf). For large PDFs (more than 10 pages), you MUST provide the pages parameter to read specific page ranges (e.g., pages: "1-5"). Reading a large PDF without the pages parameter will fail. Maximum 20 pages per request.
- This tool can read Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb files) and returns all cells with their outputs, combining code, text, and visualizations.
- This tool can only read files, not directories. To list files in a directory, use the registered shell tool.
- You will regularly be asked to read screenshots. If the user provides a path to a screenshot, ALWAYS use this tool to view the file at the path. This tool will work with all temporary file paths.
- If you read a file that exists but has empty contents you will receive a system reminder warning in place of file contents.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem.

Usage:
- This tool will overwrite the existing file if there is one at the provided path.

Если пользователь назначил новую private-серию на тех же данных, подготовь отдельное состояние и сохрани прежнюю историю по `common/isolation.md`; зафиксируй его команду и связь серий в условиях кампании. Уже полученная команда не требует повторного разрешения.
17:Зафиксируй условия трекинга. Если кампания использует MLflow для train-измерений, обеспечь исследователю чтение train-трейсов через общий сервер и проверь его на синтетической записи по `common/mlflow.md`. Сохрани разрешённый URI без секретов, experiment/run/trace ID и результат чтения payload из исследовательской среды. При обязательном MLflow недоступность train-трейсов означает незавершённую подготовку; только метрики или локальный журнал недостаточны.
19:До передачи поиска подготовь канонический журнал. При непустом private выполни проверку серверной защиты по `common/preparation.md`: режим `campaign`, авторизованный `GET /v1/search-readiness`, включённая защита, `evaluation_enabled=true` и совпадающие лимит предложений, K, N (`output_count`) и release ID. При пустом private его сервис и эта проверка не требуются. Создание пустого журнала не является поиском и не занимает места в лимите предложенных решений. Наличие `/healthz`, настройки только в env-файле или старое свидетельство не доказывают готовность защиты.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Раскладка /srv/arena для кейса AR-04а по таблице «Данные и права» из deploy/README.md арены.
# Запускает оператор: sudo bash case/deploy/stage_srv.sh
# Повторный запуск безопасен: существующие токены и журнал не перезаписываются.
set -euo pipefail

REPO="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.." && pwd)"
OPERATOR_HOME="$(getent passwd "${SUDO_USER:-$USER}" | cut -d: -f6)"
PRIVATE_SRC="${PRIVATE_SRC:-$OPERATOR_HOME/arena-private}"   # public/private от generate.py split
SRV=/srv/arena
UID_ARENA=10001   # пользователь контейнеров арены

[ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ] || { echo "нужен sudo" >&2; exit 1; }

install -d -m 0755 "$SRV"

# закрытые разделы: только оператор (root) и evaluator (UID 10001)
for split in public private; do
  install -d -m 0700 -o "$UID_ARENA" -g "$UID_ARENA" "$SRV/$split" "$SRV/$split/state" "$SRV/$split/usage"
  install -m 0400 -o "$UID_ARENA" -g "$UID_ARENA" "$PRIVATE_SRC/$split.jsonl" "$SRV/$split/dataset.jsonl"
done

# секреты: отдельный submit-токен на каждый сервис; пустой ключ модели (решатель и метрика без LLM)
install -d -m 0700 -o "$UID_ARENA" -g "$UID_ARENA" "$SRV/secrets"
for name in public-submit-token private-submit-token train-submit-token; do
  [ -s "$SRV/secrets/$name" ] || (umask 077; head -c 32 /dev/urandom | base64 | tr -d '\n' > "$SRV/secrets/$name")
done
[ -e "$SRV/secrets/model-api-key" ] || : > "$SRV/secrets/model-api-key"
chown "$UID_ARENA:$UID_ARENA" "$SRV/secrets"/* && chmod 0400 "$SRV/secrets"/*

# токены, которые получает исследователь (submit-доступ, без операторских полномочий)
install -d -m 0500 -o "$UID_ARENA" -g "$UID_ARENA" "$SRV/researcher-tokens"
for name in public-submit-token private-submit-token train-submit-token; do
  install -m 0400 -o "$UID_ARENA" -g "$UID_ARENA" "$SRV/secrets/$name" "$SRV/researcher-tokens/$name"
done

# assets: каталог и закреплённые модели, только чтение для всех кандидатов
install -d -m 0755 "$SRV/assets"
install -m 0644 "$REPO/case/assets/catalog.jsonl" "$SRV/assets/catalog.jsonl"
rsync -a --delete --chmod=D0755,F0644 "$REPO/case/assets/models/" "$SRV/assets/models/"

# журнал кампании и операторский каталог остановки
install -d -m 0700 -o "$UID_ARENA" -g "$UID_ARENA" "$SRV/search"
install -d -m 0700 "$SRV/search-control"

# HOME исследователя (логин Claude Code, транскрипты) — отдельно от HOME оператора
install -d -m 0700 -o "$UID_ARENA" -g "$UID_ARENA" "$SRV/researcher-home"

# чистая исследовательская копия: клон закоммиченного main (public/private в git нет).
# Перед тем как отдать историю исследователю — проверка утечек по всей истории main:
# данные читает root, скрипт работает под оператором.
(cd "$REPO" && cat "$PRIVATE_SRC/public.jsonl" "$PRIVATE_SRC/private.jsonl" \
  | sudo -u "${SUDO_USER:?запускайте через sudo}" python3 scripts/leak_check.py main) \
  || { echo "в истории main найден текст public/private — исследовательская копия не обновлена" >&2; exit 1; }
main_sha="$(git -c safe.directory='*' -C "$REPO" rev-parse main)"
if [ ! -d "$SRV/train/.git" ]; then
  # --no-local: в клон попадают только объекты, достижимые из main, а не весь .git/objects
  git -c safe.directory='*' clone --quiet --no-local --branch main "$REPO" "$SRV/train"
elif ! git -c safe.directory='*' -C "$SRV/train" merge-base --is-ancestor "$main_sha" HEAD 2>/dev/null; then
  # обновить до main; локальные коммиты исследователя не затираются (только fast-forward)
  git -c safe.directory='*' -C "$SRV/train" pull --quiet --ff-only origin main || {
    echo "история $SRV/train расходится с main (переписана?): удалите каталог и запустите снова" >&2; exit 1; }
fi
chown -R "$UID_ARENA:$UID_ARENA" "$SRV/train"

# замороженный пакет метрики кладёт оператор после подготовки:
#   cp -a <campaign_dir>/metric/. /srv/arena/metric/
install -d -m 0755 "$SRV/metric"

echo "готово: $SRV"
find "$SRV" -maxdepth 2 \( -path "$SRV/assets/models" -prune -o -print \) | sort | while read -r p; do
  stat -c '%A %u:%g %n' "$p"
done

OPERATOR_HOME="$(getent passwd "${SUDO_USER:-$USER}" | cut -d: -f6)"

install -d -m 0755 "$SRV"

# закрытые разделы: только оператор (root) и evaluator (UID 10001)

  install -d -m 0700 -o "$UID_ARENA" -g "$UID_ARENA" "$SRV/$split" "$SRV/$split/state" "$SRV/$split/usage"

done

install -d -m 0700 -o "$UID_ARENA" -g "$UID_ARENA" "$SRV/secrets"
for name in public-submit-token private-submit-token train-submit-token; do
  [ -s "$SRV/secrets/$name" ] || (umask 077; head -c 32 /dev/urandom | base64 | tr -d '\n' > "$SRV/secrets/$name")
done
[ -e "$SRV/secrets/model-api-key" ] || : > "$SRV/secrets/model-api-key"
chown "$UID_ARENA:$UID_ARENA" "$SRV/secrets"/* && chmod 0400 "$SRV/secrets"/*

# токены, которые получает исследователь (submit-доступ, без операторских полномочий)
install -d -m 0500 -o "$UID_ARENA" -g "$UID_ARENA" "$SRV/researcher-tokens"
for name in public-submit-token private-submit-token train-submit-token; do
  install -m 0400 -o "$UID_ARENA" -g "$UID_ARENA" "$SRV/secrets/$name" "$SRV/researcher-tokens/$name"
done

# assets: каталог и закреплённые модели, только чтение для всех кандидатов
install -d -m 0755 "$SRV/assets"
install -m 0644 "$REPO/case/assets/catalog.jsonl" "$SRV/assets/catalog.jsonl"
rsync -a --delete --chmod=D0755,F0644 "$REPO/case/assets/models/" "$SRV/assets/models/"

# журнал кампании и операторский каталог остановки
install -d -m 0700 -o "$UID_ARENA" -g "$UID_ARENA" "$SRV/search"
install -d -m 0700 "$SRV/search-control"

install -d -m 0700 -o "$UID_ARENA" -g "$UID_ARENA" "$SRV/researcher-home"

# чистая исследовательская копия: клон закоммиченного main (public/private в git нет).
# Перед тем как отдать историю исследователю — проверка утечек по всей истории main:

  | sudo -u "${SUDO_USER:?запускайте через sudo}" python3 scripts/leak_check.py main) \
  || { echo "в истории main найден текст public/private — исследовательская копия не обновлена" >&2; exit 1; }
main_sha="$(git -c safe.directory='*' -C "$REPO" rev-parse main)"
if [ ! -d "$SRV/train/.git" ]; then
  # --no-local: в клон попадают только объекты, достижимые из main, а не весь .git/objects

elif ! git -c safe.directory='*' -C "$SRV/train" merge-base --is-ancestor "$main_sha" HEAD 2>/dev/null; then
  # обновить до main; локальные коммиты исследователя не затираются (только fast-forward)
  git -c safe.directory='*' -C "$SRV/train" pull --quiet --ff-only origin main || {
    echo "история $SRV/train расходится с main (переписана?): удалите каталог и запустите снова" >&2; exit 1; }

chown -R "$UID_ARENA:$UID_ARENA" "$SRV/train"

# замороженный пакет метрики кладёт оператор после подготовки:
#   cp -a <campaign_dir>/metric/. /srv/arena/metric/
install -d -m 0755 "$SRV/metric"

echo "готово: $SRV"

  stat -c '%A %u:%g %n' "$p"

content.content:
# Развёртывание кейса AR-04а (для оператора)

Общий порядок, роли и права — по [deploy/README.md](https://gitlab.deeppavlov.ai/deeppavlov/arena/-/blob/a28eee3/deploy/README.md) и [common/isolation.md](https://gitlab.deeppavlov.ai/deeppavlov/arena/-/blob/a28eee3/common/isolation.md) арены, коммит `a28eee3`. Здесь только значения нашего кейса: арена отводит под них `cases/<case>/deploy/`. Почему так и чем отличается от арены — [ADR-0006](../../docs/adr/0006-isolation.md).

```
 оператор (WSL, mikhart)           доверенный контур                         исследователь
 ───────────────────────           ─────────────────                         ─────────────
 stage_srv.sh → /srv/arena   ──►  evaluator public  :8090 ┐                 контейнер researcher
                                  evaluator private :8080 ├─ runner ──►     (compose profile train)
                                  train-сервис      :8070 ┘  ar04a-runner   Claude Code + start.md
                                  данные /srv/arena/{public,private}        видит: /workspace (train),
                                                                            /search (журнал), токены
                                  ◄─────── кандидат по HTTP + токен ─────── 
                                  ───────► public: score, private: статус ─►
```

## Файлы

| файл | что это |
|---|---|
| [stage_srv.sh](stage_srv.sh) | раскладка `/srv/arena` по таблице «Данные и права» арены (через sudo) |
| [public.env.example](public.env.example), [private.env.example](private.env.example) | операторские env двух оценщиков (ключи как в `deploy/operator.env.example`) |
| [runner.Dockerfile](runner.Dockerfile) | runner арены + библиотеки кейса из `uv.lock` |
| [researcher.Dockerfile](researcher.Dockerfile) | контейнер исследователя арены + Claude Code (харнес добавляет оператор) |
| [compose.override.yaml](compose.override.yaml) | образ исследователя, постоянный HOME (логин и транскрипты), адреса оценщиков, submit-токены |
| [check_isolation.sh](check_isolation.sh) | проверка границы изнутри контейнера исследователя |

## Шаги

Все команды `docker compose` выполняются в `~/arena`, `$REPO` — этот репозиторий. Порядок — как в `deploy/README.md` арены: подготовка замораживает метрику, оператор устанавливает пакет и запускает сервисы, затем подготовка подтверждает готовность, и только после этого идёт отдельный запуск поиска.

1. **Данные и права.** Повторный запуск `stage_srv.sh` обновляет `/srv/arena/train` до текущего `main`.
   ```bash
   uv run python case/assets/fetch_models.py           # если моделей ещё нет
   sudo bash case/deploy/stage_srv.sh
   ```
2. **Env.** Скопировать `public.env.example` и `private.env.example` в `/etc/arena/`, заполнить `TODO`.
3. **Образы.**
   ```bash
   docker compose --env-file /etc/arena/private.env --profile private build
   docker compose --env-file /etc/arena/private.env --profile train build researcher
   docker build -t arena-runner:local -f runner/Dockerfile .
   docker build -t ar04a-runner:local -f $REPO/case/deploy/runner.Dockerfile $REPO
   docker build -t ar04a-researcher:local -f $REPO/case/deploy/researcher.Dockerfile $REPO/case/deploy
   ```
4. **Подготовка кампании** — отдельный запуск Claude Code с `prompts/prepare.md` арены в контейнере `researcher` (команда та же, что в шаге 8), условия — [campaign.md](../campaign/campaign.md). Не на хосте: под учёткой оператора агенту доступны транскрипты сессии, генерировавшей данные (`~/.claude`), а в них есть запросы private; агенту подготовки арена разрешает только открытые и синтетические данные (`common/isolation.md`). #!/usr/bin/env bash
# Проверка границы закрытых данных ИЗНУТРИ контейнера исследователя (common/isolation.md арены).
# Запуск оператором:
#   docker compose -f compose.yaml -f <repo>/case/deploy/compose.override.yaml \
#     --env-file /etc/arena/private.env --profile train run --rm researcher \
#     bash /workspace/case/deploy/check_isolation.sh
# Каждая строка должна быть OK; вывод сохраняется в <campaign_dir>/preparation.md.
set -u
fail=0
ok()  { echo "OK    $*"; }
bad() { echo "FAIL  $*"; fail=1; }
absent() { if [ -e "$1" ]; then bad "доступно: $1"; else ok "нет доступа: $1"; fi; }

echo "uid=$(id -u) gid=$(id -g) groups=$(id -G)"
[ "$(id -u)" != 0 ] && ok "не root" || bad "работает от root"

# закрытые данные, состояние оценщиков, секреты и операторские каталоги не смонтированы
for p in /srv/arena /private /state /usage /search-control /run/secrets/model-api-key \
         /srv/arena/secrets /home/mikhart /etc/arena; do absent "$p"; done

# управление хостом: docker socket, docker CLI, sudo, выход в Windows (WSL interop)
absent /var/run/docker.sock
command -v docker >/dev/null && bad "есть docker CLI" || ok "нет docker CLI"
command -v sudo   >/dev/null && bad "есть sudo"       || ok "нет sudo"
command -v wsl.exe >/dev/null && bad "есть wsl.exe"   || ok "нет wsl.exe"
absent /mnt/c

# public/private-данные не лежат в рабочей копии (их хеши — в case/dataset/generation_report.md)
for name in public private; do
  hits=$(find /workspace /search /home/researcher -name "${name}.jsonl" -o -name "${name}.meta.jsonl" 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
  [ "$hits" = 0 ] && ok "нет ${name}.jsonl в рабочих каталогах" || bad "найден ${name}.jsonl"
done

# операторские переменные окружения не переданы
env | grep -qE '^ARENA_(DATASET_PATH|STATE_DIR|USAGE_DIR|MODEL_API_KEY_FILE|SUBMIT_TOKEN_FILE)=' \
  && bad "в окружении операторские ARENA_*" || ok "нет операторских ARENA_* в окружении"

# исследователю разрешено: train, журнал, submit-токены
[ -r /workspace/case/dataset/train.jsonl ] && ok "train доступен" || bad "train недоступен"
[ -w /search ] && ok "журнал /search доступен на запись" || bad "/search недоступен"
ls /run/secrets/arena/ >/dev/null 2>&1 && ok "submit-токены доступны: $(ls /run/secrets/arena | tr '\n' ' ')" \
  || bad "нет submit-токенов"

exit $fail

from evaluator.search import Journal, SearchError
from evaluator.tracking import export_configured

MAX_BODY_BYTES = 70 * 1024 * 1024


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Settings:
    dataset_path: Path
    metric_path: Path
    state_dir: Path
    token: str = field(repr=False)
    runner_image: str
    release_id: str
    model: str = ""
    model_base_url: str = ""
    model_api_key: str = field(default="", repr=False)
    runner_network: str = "none"
    runner_model_base_url: str = "http://model-gateway:8081/v1"
    runner_timeout: float = RUNNER_TIMEOUT
    model_timeout: float = MODEL_TIMEOUT
    prepare_timeout: float = PREPARE_TIMEOUT
    retry_delay: float = RETRY_DELAY
    usage_dir: Path | None = None
    assets_dir: Path | None = None
    finalists: int = 5
    output_count: int = 1
    split: str = "private"
    uses_model: bool = True
    harnesses: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = field(default_factory=dict)
    max_body_bytes: int | None = None
    parameters: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    runner_memory: str = "2g"
    runner_cpus: str = "2"
    runner_pids_limit: int = 128
    runner_tmpfs_size: str = "128m"
    runner_tmpfs_exec: bool = False
    trace_dir: Path | None = None
    tracking_dir: Path | None = None
    tracking_queue_dir: Path | None = None
    case_id: str = ""
    slot_dir: Path | None = None
    execution_slots: int = 4
    published_assets_dir: Path | None = None
    build_dir: Path | None = None
    input_assets_digest: str | None = None
    runner_supports_build: bool = False
    runner_supports_asset_selection: bool = False
    asset_staging_dir: Path | None = None
    asset_store_dir: Path | None = None
    search_mode: str = "standalone"
    search_journal: Path | None = None
    search_max_solutions: int | None = None
    search_stop_path: Path | None = None

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if any(not value.strip() for value in (self.token, self.runner_image, self.release_id)):
            raise ValueError("token, runner image and release ID are required")
        if type(self.finalists) is not int or self.finalists < 1:
            raise ValueError("finalists must be a positive integer")
        if type(self.output_count) is not int or not 1 <= self.output_count <= self.finalists:
            raise ValueError("output_count must be between 1 and finalists")
        if self.split not in {"private", "public"}:
            raise ValueError("split must be private or public")
        if self.search_mode not in {"standalone", "campaign"}:
            raise ValueError("search mode must be standalone or campaign")
        if self.search_mode == "campaign" and self.search_journal is None:
            raise ValueError("search campaign requires a journal and max_solutions")
        if self.search_mode == "standalone" and self.search_journal is not None:
            raise ValueError("search journal requires campaign mode")
        if (self.search_journal is None) != (self.search_max_solutions is None):
            raise ValueError("search journal and max_solutions must be configured together")
        if self.search_max_solutions is not None and (
            type(self.search_max_solutions) is not int or self.search_max_solutions < 1
        ):
            raise ValueError("search max_solutions must be a positive integer")
        if self.search_stop_path is not None and self.search_journal is None:
            raise ValueError("search stop path requires a search journal")
        for name in ("uses_model", "runner_supports_build", "runner_supports_asset_selection"):
            if type(getattr(self, name)) is not bool:
                raise ValueError(f"{name} must be a boolean")
        if (self.asset_staging_dir is None) != (self.asset_store_dir is None):
            raise ValueError("asset staging and store directories must be configured together")
        if self.max_body_bytes is not None and (
            type(self.max_body_bytes) is not int or self.max_body_bytes < 1
        ):
            raise ValueError("max_body_bytes must be a positive integer")
        if not isinstance(self.harnesses, dict):
            raise ValueError("harnesses must be a JSON object")
        for name, config in self.harnesses.items():
            if (
                not isinstance(name, str) or not name.strip()
                or not isinstance(config, dict)
                or set(config) - {"image", "uses_model", "network",
                                  "supports_build", "supports_asset_selection"}
                or not isinstance(config.get("image"), str) or not config["image"].strip()
                or type(config.get("uses_model", self.uses_model)) is not bool
                or type(config.get("supports_build", False)) is not bool
                or type(config.get("supports_asset_selection", False)) is not bool
                or not isinstance(config.get("network", self.runner_network), str)
            ):
                raise ValueError("invalid harness registry")
        if (self.uses_model or any(
            config.get("uses_model", self.uses_model) for config in self.harnesses.values()
        )) and (not self.model.strip() or not self.model_base_url.strip()):
            raise ValueError("model and endpoint are required for model-based harnesses")
        for name in ("runner_timeout", "model_timeout", "prepare_timeout"):
            validate_timing(getattr(self, name), name)
        validate_timing(self.retry_delay, "retry_delay", allow_zero=True)
        validate_runner_resources(
            self.runner_memory, self.runner_cpus, self.runner_pids_limit,
            self.runner_tmpfs_size, self.runner_tmpfs_exec,
        )
        if not isinstance(self.parameters, dict):
            raise ValueError("parameters must be a JSON object")
        if self.tracking_dir is not None and not self.case_id.strip():
            raise ValueError("case_id is required for tracking export")
        if type(self.execution_slots) is not int or self.execution_slots < 1:
            raise ValueError("execution_slots must be a positive integer")

    @classmethod
    def from_env(cls) -> "Settings":
        def value(name: str, default: str | None = None) -> str:
            name = "ARENA_" + name
            path = os.environ.get(name + "_FILE")
            if path:
                return Path(path).read_text().strip()
            result = os.environ.get(name, default)
            if result is None:
                raise ValueError(f"{name} is required")
            return result

        assets = value("ASSETS_DIR", "")
        usage = value("USAGE_DIR", "")
        trace = value("TRACE_DIR", "")
        tracking = value("TRACKING_DIR", "")
        tracking_queue = value("TRACKING_QUEUE_DIR", "")
        slots = value("SLOT_DIR", "")
        published_assets = value("PUBLISHED_ASSETS_DIR", "")
        builds = value("BUILD_DIR", "")
        asset_staging = value("ASSET_STAGING_DIR", "")
        asset_store = value("ASSET_STORE_DIR", "")
        search_journal = value("SEARCH_JOURNAL", "")
        search_max_solutions = value("SEARCH_MAX_SOLUTIONS", "")
        search_stop = value("SEARCH_STOP_PATH", "")
        capabilities = {}
        for name in ("RUNNER_SUPPORTS_BUILD", "RUNNER_SUPPORTS_ASSET_SELECTION"):
            enabled = value(name, "false").lower()
            if enabled not in {"true", "false"}:
                raise ValueError(f"ARENA_{name} must be true or false")
            capabilities[name.lower()] = enabled == "true"
        uses_model = value("USES_MODEL", "true").lower()
        if uses_model not in {"true", "false"}:
            raise ValueError("ARENA_USES_MODEL must be true or false")
        tmpfs_exec = value("RUNNER_TMPFS_EXEC", "false").lower()
        if tmpfs_exec not in {"true", "false"}:
            raise ValueError("ARENA_RUNNER_TMPFS_EXEC must be true or false")
        body_bytes = value("MAX_BODY_BYTES", "")
        return cls(
            dataset_path=Path(value("DATASET_PATH")),
            metric_path=Path(value("METRIC_PATH")),
            state_dir=Path(value("STATE_DIR")),
            token=value("TOKEN"),
            model=value("MODEL", ""),
            model_base_url=value("MODEL_BASE_URL", ""),
            runner_image=value("RUNNER_IMAGE"),
            release_id=value("RELEASE_ID"),
            model_api_key=value("MODEL_API_KEY", ""),
            runner_network=value("RUNNER_NETWORK", "none"),
            runner_model_base_url=value("RUNNER_MODEL_BASE_URL", "http://model-gateway:8081/v1"),
            runner_timeout=float(value("RUNNER_TIMEOUT", str(RUNNER_TIMEOUT))),
            model_timeout=float(value("MODEL_TIMEOUT", str(MODEL_TIMEOUT))),
            prepare_timeout=float(value("PREPARE_TIMEOUT", str(PREPARE_TIMEOUT))),
            retry_delay=float(value("RETRY_DELAY", str(RETRY_DELAY))),
            usage_dir=Path(usage) if usage else None,
            assets_dir=Path(assets) if assets else None,
            finalists=int(value("FINALISTS", "5")),
            output_count=int(value("OUTPUT_COUNT", "1")),
            split=value("SPLIT", "private"),
            uses_model=uses_model == "true",
            harnesses=json.loads(value("HARNESSES", "{}")),
            max_body_bytes=int(body_bytes) if body_bytes else None,
            parameters=json.loads(value("PARAMETERS", "{}")),
            runner_memory=value("RUNNER_MEMORY", "2g"),
            runner_cpus=value("RUNNER_CPUS", "2"),
            runner_pids_limit=int(value("RUNNER_PIDS_LIMIT", "128")),
            runner_tmpfs_size=value("RUNNER_TMPFS_SIZE", "128m"),
            runner_tmpfs_exec=tmpfs_exec == "true",
            trace_dir=Path(trace) if trace else None,
            tracking_dir=Path(tracking) if tracking else None,
            tracking_queue_dir=Path(tracking_queue) if tracking_queue else None,
            case_id=value("CASE_ID", ""),
            slot_dir=Path(slots) if slots else None,
            execution_slots=int(value("EXECUTION_SLOTS", "4")),
            published_assets_dir=Path(published_assets) if published_assets else None,
            build_dir=Path(builds) if builds else None,
            input_assets_digest=value("INPUT_ASSETS_DIGEST", "") or None,
            asset_staging_dir=Path(asset_staging) if asset_staging else None,
            asset_store_dir=Path(asset_store) if asset_store else None,
            search_mode=value("SEARCH_MODE", "standalone"),
            search_journal=Path(search_journal) if search_journal else None,
    evaluate_answer,
)
from evaluator.reliability import MODEL_RETRIES, add_usage, empty_usage, validate_timing
from evaluator.runner import HarnessRunner, RunnerError, SolveResult

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TrainSettings:
    evaluation: Settings
    campaign_id: str
    case_id: str
    dataset_id: str
    conditions_id: str
    tracking: bool = True

    @classmethod
    def from_env(cls) -> "TrainSettings":
        tracking = os.getenv("ARENA_TRAIN_TRACKING", "true") == "true"
        return cls(Settings.from_env(), tracking=tracking, **{
            name: os.environ["ARENA_" + name.upper()]
            for name in ("campaign_id", "case_id", "dataset_id", "conditions_id")
        })


class TrainSubmission(StrictModel):
    candidate: Candidate
    example_ids: list[str] | None = Field(default=None, min_length=1)
    metadata: dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)


def _digest(value: Any) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(
        value, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), allow_nan=False,
    ).encode()).hexdigest()


def _clean(value: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    encoded = json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, allow_nan=False)
    encoded = re.sub(r"(/runs/[a-f0-9-]{36}/)[a-f0-9]{64}(/v1)", r"\1[redacted]\2", encoded)
    return json.loads(encoded)


def _save(path: Path, record: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    _write_json(path, _clean(record))


def _metrics(record: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    metrics = dict(record.get("metrics", {}))
    if record["status"] == "FAILED":
        metrics.pop("score", None)
    for role in ("solver", "judge"):
        resources = [item["resources"][role] for item in record["examples"]]
        if role == "solver" and record.get("preparation") is not None:
            resources.append(record["preparation"]["resources"]["solver"])
        if role == "judge" and "resources" in record.get("aggregation", {}):
            resources.append(record["aggregation"]["resources"]["judge"])
        metrics[f"{role}_tokens"] = sum(item["usage"]["total_tokens"] for item in resources)
        metrics[f"{role}_seconds"] = sum(item["wall_seconds"] for item in resources)
        metrics[f"{role}_unreported_attempts"] = sum(
            item["usage"]["unreported_attempts"] for item in resources
        )
        metrics[f"{role}_resources_complete"] = all(
            item.get("usage_complete", True) and item.get("wall_seconds_complete", True)
            for item in resources
        )
    metrics["wall_seconds"] = (time.time_ns() - record["start_time_ns"]) / 1e9
    return metrics


def _call(
    record: dict[str, Any], role: str, started: int, inputs: Any, outputs: Any,
    *, example_id: str | None = None, failed: bool = False,
) -> None:
    record["calls"].append({
        "name": role, "inputs": inputs, "outputs": outputs,
        "attributes": {"role": role, "example_id": example_id},
        "status": "ERROR" if failed else "OK", "start_time_ns": started,
        "end_time_ns": time.time_ns(),
    })

        for name in ("uses_model", "runner_supports_build", "runner_supports_asset_selection"):
            if type(getattr(self, name)) is not bool:
                raise ValueError(f"{name} must be a boolean")
        if (self.asset_staging_dir is None) != (self.asset_store_dir is None):
            raise ValueError("asset staging and store directories must be configured together")
        if self.max_body_bytes is not None and (
            type(self.max_body_bytes) is not int or self.max_body_bytes < 1
        ):
            raise ValueError("max_body_bytes must be a positive integer")
        if not isinstance(self.harnesses, dict):
            raise ValueError("harnesses must be a JSON object")
        for name, config in self.harnesses.items():
            if (
                not isinstance(name, str) or not name.strip()
                or not isinstance(config, dict)
                or set(config) - {"image", "uses_model", "network",
                                  "supports_build", "supports_asset_selection"}
                or not isinstance(config.get("image"), str) or not config["image"].strip()
                or type(config.get("uses_model", self.uses_model)) is not bool
                or type(config.get("supports_build", False)) is not bool
                or type(config.get("supports_asset_selection", False)) is not bool
                or not isinstance(config.get("network", self.runner_network), str)
            ):
                raise ValueError("invalid harness registry")
        if (self.uses_model or any(
            config.get("uses_model", self.uses_model) for config in self.harnesses.values()
        )) and (not self.model.strip() or not self.model_base_url.strip()):

        validate_runner_resources(

            self.runner_tmpfs_size, self.runner_tmpfs_exec,

        if not isinstance(self.parameters, dict):
            raise ValueError("parameters must be a JSON object")
        if self.tracking_dir is not None and not self.case_id.strip():
            raise ValueError("case_id is required for tracking export")
        if type(self.execution_slots) is not int or self.execution_slots < 1:
            raise ValueError("execution_slots must be a positive integer")

def _digest(value: Any) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(
        value, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), allow_nan=False,
    ).encode()).hexdigest()


def _clean(value: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    encoded = json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, allow_nan=False)
    encoded = re.sub(r"(/runs/[a-f0-9-]{36}/)[a-f0-9]{64}(/v1)", r"\1[redacted]\2", encoded)
    return json.loads(encoded)


def _save(path: Path, record: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    _write_json(path, _clean(record))


def _metrics(record: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    metrics = dict(record.get("metrics", {}))
    if record["status"] == "FAILED":
        metrics.pop("score", None)
    for role in ("solver", "judge"):
        resources = [item["resources"][role] for item in record["examples"]]
        if role == "solver" and record.get("preparation") is not None:
            resources.append(record["preparation"]["resources"]["solver"])
        if role == "judge" and "resources" in record.get("aggregation", {}):
            resources.append(record["aggregation"]["resources"]["judge"])
        metrics[f"{role}_tokens"] = sum(item["usage"]["total_tokens"] for item in resources)
        metrics[f"{role}_seconds"] = sum(item["wall_seconds"] for item in resources)
        metrics[f"{role}_unreported_attempts"] = sum(
            item["usage"]["unreported_attempts"] for item in resources
        )
        metrics[f"{role}_resources_complete"] = all(
            item.get("usage_complete", True) and item.get("wall_seconds_complete", True)
            for item in resources
        )
    metrics["wall_seconds"] = (time.time_ns() - record["start_time_ns"]) / 1e9
    return metrics


def _call(
    record: dict[str, Any], role: str, started: int, inputs: Any, outputs: Any,
    *, example_id: str | None = None, failed: bool = False,
) -> None:
    record["calls"].append({
        "name": role, "inputs": inputs, "outputs": outputs,
        "attributes": {"role": role, "example_id": example_id},
        "status": "ERROR" if failed else "OK", "start_time_ns": started,
        "end_time_ns": time.time_ns(),
    })

Команда `result` дополнительно принимает `--journal`, `--measurement` и `--output`, сохраняет завершённый результат и связывает его с замером. `--example-id` у `submit` выбирает train-подвыборку. Повторные замеры неизменного кандидата используют уже полученные корректные ответы; отсутствие MLflow не препятствует измерению.

Train-сервис может дополнительно предоставить publisher и build API. Они не включаются общим Compose автоматически: нужен отдельный сервис или Compose override, который передаёт флаги возможностей и пути хранилищ оценщику и монтирует соответствующие каталоги. Одного изменения `operator.env` недостаточно. Оператор задаёт `ARENA_ASSET_STAGING_DIR` для доступного исследователю staging, `ARENA_ASSET_STORE_DIR` для доверенного неизменяемого хранилища, `ARENA_BUILD_DIR` для закрытых квитанций и `ARENA_INPUT_ASSETS_DIGEST` для закреплённых исходных материалов. Runner и eval-сервисы получают это же хранилище через `ARENA_PUBLISHED_ASSETS_DIR` и одинаковые настройки харнеса. Исследователь не получает запись в публикации, квитанции или Docker socket. Общий предел одновременного исполнения задают `ARENA_SLOT_DIR` и `ARENA_EXECUTION_SLOTS`.

```bash
uv run python -m evaluator.assets publish \
  --url https://train-evaluator.example --token-file /run/secrets/train-submit \
  --path allowed-import
uv run python -m evaluator.build submit \
  --url https://train-evaluator.example --token-file /run/secrets/train-submit \
  --journal cases/my-case/campaigns/my-campaign/search.sqlite --candidate way-a
uv run python -m evaluator.build status \
  --url https://train-evaluator.example --token-file /run/secrets/train-submit \
  --digest '<candidate-digest>'
```

`ARENA_BUILD_DIR` обязателен при `supports_asset_selection: true`, даже если разрешены только готовые веса и `supports_build: false`. Это общий доверенный журнал квитанций и связей для данного хранилища публикаций. Пустой каталог вместо существующего журнала не допускается: потеря связей не должна превращать оплачиваемую подготовку в бесплатный импорт. Каталог и файлы журнала принадлежат UID оценщика, не доступны для записи группе или остальным пользователям и не являются символическими ссылками.

Train-сервис создаёт журнал через `BuildStore` при старте с настроенными `ARENA_BUILD_DIR`, `ARENA_PUBLISHED_ASSETS_DIR` и `ARENA_INPUT_ASSETS_DIGEST`. Запустите его до закрытых оценщиков: они проверяют уже созданную конфигурацию. Для нового развёртывания без train-сервиса оператор может выполнить следующую инициализацию в окружении оценщика, с его окончательными переменными `ARENA_*` и UID:

```python
from evaluator.build import BuildStore, run_build
from evaluator.build_receipts import build_environment
from evaluator.execution import make_runner
from evaluator.service import Settings

settings = Settings.from_env()
if (settings.build_dir is None or settings.published_assets_dir is None
        or settings.input_assets_digest is None):
    raise ValueError("Configure receipt storage, published assets and input digest")
runner = make_runner(settings, settings.usage_dir or settings.state_dir / "usage")
BuildStore(
    settings.build_dir, settings.published_assets_dir, settings.input_assets_digest,
    build_environment(runner, settings.parameters),
    lambda candidate, output: run_build(runner, candidate, output),
    dependency_assets=runner.build_asset_digests,
)
```

Конструктор создаёт `configuration.json`, `receipts/`, `jobs/` и `bindings/`; вручную писать конфигурацию не нужно. Сам этот вызов не собирает кандидата, не запускает Docker и не обращается к модели. Отпечаток окружения вычисляется из того же реестра харнесов и параметров, которые будут у оценщиков. Не создавайте другой журнал для прежнего хранилища и не переинициализируйте состояние работающей кампании.

Путь публикации относителен staging; API не принимает произвольный путь хоста. Build требует зарегистрированного кандидата и выбранного харнеса с `supports_build: true`. Операция, mounts, квитанции версии 2 и обязательный учёт зависимостей описаны в [общем контракте](../common/runner-contract.md). Новый формат предназначен для новых развёртываний: не заменяйте квитанции или runtime уже работающей кампании.

Docker-монитор завершения внешнего исследователя вынесен в [необязательную интеграцию](../integrations/docker/README.md): `python -m integrations.docker.research_monitor`. Его конфигурация и доступ к Docker остаются у оператора; конкретная топология не является частью протокола оценки.

## Инструменты и проверка JSON в gateway

Gateway принимает от 1 до 10 000 сообщений в одном запросе; отдельно действует предел тела запроса, по умолчанию 16 MiB.

"""sha256 содержимого каталога: ARENA_INPUT_ASSETS_DIGEST и digest пакета метрики для ARENA_RELEASE_ID.

Считается по отсортированным парам (относительный путь, sha256 файла); символические ссылки не допускаются.
Запуск: python tree_digest.py <каталог> [--exclude имя ...]
"""
import argparse
import hashlib
import sys
from pathlib import Path


def tree_digest(root: Path, exclude: frozenset[str] = frozenset()) -> str:
    outer = hashlib.sha256()
    for path in sorted(root.rglob("*")):
        relative = path.relative_to(root)
        if relative.parts[0] in exclude or path.is_dir():
            continue
        if path.is_symlink() or not path.is_file():
            raise ValueError(f"только обычные файлы: {relative}")
        inner = hashlib.sha256()
        with path.open("rb") as stream:
            for block in iter(lambda: stream.read(1 << 20), b""):
                inner.update(block)
        outer.update(f"{relative.as_posix()}\0{inner.hexdigest()}\n".encode())
    return outer.hexdigest()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("directory", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--exclude", action="append", default=[], help="имя элемента верхнего уровня")
    arguments = parser.parse_args()
    if not arguments.directory.is_dir():
        sys.exit(f"нет каталога: {arguments.directory}")
    print(tree_digest(arguments.directory, frozenset(arguments.exclude)))
